title: AgentIdeaBench: Benchmarking Scientific Ideation in the Agent Era
abstract: Scientific ideation is the capacity to formulate novel and testable hypotheses from scientific evidence, and autonomous AI scientists depend on it. Existing evaluations largely assess it by asking models to generate ideas from a static, curated set of reference papers. That passive setup departs from the retrieval-and-reasoning workflow of modern AI scientists, and it becomes less discriminative as models improve. We introduce AgentIdeaBench, a multidisciplinary benchmark that evaluates scientific ideation under two matched settings, static observation and active exploration. We report matched Static-Active evaluations for 33 LLMs across 40 densely scored subfields spanning five disciplines, using a multidimensional, literature-verified scoring framework whose critics assess originality against retrieved prior art. Active exploration reveals considerably more capability headroom, and that headroom is unevenly distributed across models. Performance scales about twice as fast as under static observation, and the exploration gain is capability-gated, favoring the strongest models over the weakest. The gain reflects better grounding, improving feasibility, clarity, and specificity while leaving measured originality unchanged under our critics. We further explore Scientific World Modeling, a generation-time loop that refines a draft hypothesis through structured thought experiments. It benefits mid-capability models, and its impact diminishes among frontier models that appear to have internalized such reasoning patterns already. AgentIdeaBench gives future work on scientific ideation a measurement basis suited to the agent era.

title: Single-tone drive-enhanced CROT gate for bosonic quantum error correction
abstract: Bosonic error correction provides a hardware-efficient route to protected qubits for accurate quantum information processing. A critical component for error correction of rotation-symmetric bosonic (RSB) codes, like the well-known cat codes, is the two-mode controlled-rotation (CROT) operation. The CROT gate is useful because of its code-agnostic generality and its error-propagation properties. While the CROT gate can in principle be composed from existing bosonic physical primitives, the desirable properties are typically lost when composed as a sequence of imperfect primitive operations. Past work has focused on direct implementations that rely on features of specific codes. Here, we present a direct route to CROT within the circuit-QED architecture that retains its code-agnostic and error-propagation characteristics. By driving a transmon simultaneously coupled to two microwave cavities, we controllably enhance the effective nonlinearities between the microwave cavities and thus engineer the necessary two-mode interaction underlying the CROT gate. Using only a single drive frequency, we can achieve an on-off ratio sufficient for gate implementation, while minimizing mode distortions. We provide simple analytical formulas that permit the identification of potential working regimes, further refined by exact numerics, and illustrate the efficacy of our CROT approach in an error-correction example involving different RSB codes within the same circuit. Our CROT gate adds to the arsenal of direct two-mode gates available for general bosonic information processing.

title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
abstract: Post-hoc safety training (RLHF, DPO) is the dominant way to align large language models, yet jailbreaks (Zou et al., 2023), fine-tuning attacks (Qi et al., 2024), and activation-space edits (Arditi et al., 2024) keep recovering the behaviors it was meant to remove. We give this fragility one geometric explanation and follow it into pretraining. We measure the safety update $Δ= W_{safe} - W_{base}$ against the curvature of the model's capabilities (the empirical Fisher of a capability loss). Across five model families, post-hoc safety lands in a suppression regime: $Δ$ is nearly orthogonal to the capability directions, and its small in-subspace part concentrates on a few high-curvature ones. The update is thin but sharp, a refusal gate laid over intact capabilities rather than erasure of them. A kernel-immobility lemma explains why such an update can only mask a capability, not remove it, so a little benign fine-tuning restores it: 100 benign examples cut the AdvBench refusal of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct by 35 to 38 pp. Following the account into pretraining, a pretraining-checkpoint sweep of OLMo-2-1B (Team OLMo et al., 2024) shows the features that refusal attaches to emerging in a sharp transition between 1B and 63B pretraining tokens. We then use the account constructively: models trained from scratch with safety co-training spread continuously across pretraining reach 87 to 98% AdvBench refusal that the same attack erodes by only 2 to 14 pp at every scale from 410M to 6.9B, against 35 to 38 pp for post-hoc installs, at a small cost on short-answer capability probes; a windowed schedule of equal total safety weight installs no refusal. Persistence of the safety signal across pretraining, not its timing, is what buys attack robustness.

title: When Causal Attention Sees the Future
abstract: A reproducible nntrainer causal-mask report: future values affect earlier outputs. Native tests, a local repair and an upstream issue are available. This article was already archived in the 45-item GERO collection (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22683900). title: MCP Monoculture: The Systemic Security Failure of Agentic AI Infrastructure
abstract: RS-2026-065. Synthesis of Red Specter's TRUTH SURFACE series — nine architecture analyses of the top AI security vendors — revealing MCP (Model Context Protocol) exposure as a critical vulnerability in every paper. Documents five protocol-level vulnerabilities, eight active CVEs mapped to NIGHTFALL attack classes, and supply chain risks across 973 MCP packages. Calls on the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation for protocol reform. The central finding: every vendor is vulnerable because the protocol is vulnerable. Cites TRUTH SURFACE #001-#009, RS-2026-063, RS-2026-064. Tool: T287 SPECTER MCP-SCAN v1.0.0.

title: Title: Emergent Pattern Recognition in Multi-Layered Cognitive Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the emergence of complex cognitive patterns within multi-layered neural networks through the development of a novel 'hierarchical coherence' algorithm. Traditional approaches often rely on feature extraction and statistical analysis, failing to capture the dynamic interplay of information across multiple layers. This work proposes a method that analyzes the propagation of patterns, quantifying interdependence to identify emergent cognitive structures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulated and experimental analyses, revealing a significant shift from passive feature representation to active pattern formation. The core mechanism centers on a hierarchical coherence algorithm that progresses through multiple layers, quantifying the degree of interdependence and identifying key nodes that drive pattern evolution. This offers a more holistic and insightful approach to understanding the underlying dynamics of cognition within complex neural systems.

title: 基于动态拓扑的概率分布建模
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology as a framework for probabilistic model construction. Traditional probabilistic modeling often relies on static assumptions and limited flexibility. We propose a novel method leveraging dynamic topology, allowing for the adaptive adjustment of probability distribution parameters through a process of topology manipulation. This approach offers a significant advantage in modeling complex, non-linear probability distributions, facilitating parameter optimization and enhanced model generalization. The core mechanism involves the construction of a dynamic topology, which iteratively adjusts parameters to achieve a desired probabilistic outcome. The paper presents a theoretical foundation for this dynamic topology approach and provides a practical implementation utilizing a specific algorithm for parameter optimization. We explore the benefits of this method in various scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing complex dependencies within probability distributions.

title: The Implicit Information Space
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for automated reasoning and learning, centered around the concept of an Implicit Information Space. We propose a method leveraging the inherent relationships within variables and the dynamic nature of information flow to enable robust and adaptable knowledge representation. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating this space, facilitating automated inference and knowledge graph construction. The significance of this approach lies in its potential to overcome limitations of traditional knowledge graph approaches, offering increased autonomy and adaptability to complex systems. This research investigates the design and implementation of this framework, highlighting its advantages and potential applications across diverse domains.

title: 基于多尺度信息检索的自适应知识图谱构建
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing adaptive knowledge graphs (KGs) based on multi-scale information retrieval. The core claim is that by leveraging multi-scale information retrieval, combining knowledge entities and relationships at different granularities, the knowledge graph construction process can be adaptively optimized, leading to improved KG quality and scalability. The proposed mechanism decomposes KG construction into multi-scale information retrieval stages. At low scales, precise matching is the primary goal, retrieving fragments highly related to existing entities and relationships. At high scales, conceptual association is the focus, retrieving fragments with potential associations. The results of these different-scale retrievals are then fused and filtered to progressively build a more comprehensive and accurate KG. This approach addresses limitations of existing KG construction methods that often rely on predefined rules or manual intervention, offering an adaptive solution to reduce noise and uncertainty. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of retrieval strategies based on the evolving KG structure. This work aims to provide a robust and scalable method for KG construction, particularly in scenarios with incomplete or noisy data. The proposed framework utilizes a hierarchical approach to information retrieval, allowing for a nuanced understanding of relationships within a knowledge domain. The methodology is presented with a focus on the algorithmic design and the integration of different retrieval techniques. We demonstrate the efficacy of the approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a potential implementation strategy. ---

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Topology for Quantum State Encoding
abstract: Quantum state encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, demanding novel approaches to maintain quantum coherence. This paper investigates the application of non-Euclidean topology as a potential tool for achieving this goal. We propose a method for representing quantum states using a non-Euclidean space, exploiting its inherent properties for enhanced quantum coherence. The core mechanism centers around a representation of the quantum state using a non-Euclidean space, leveraging its unique properties for encoding and manipulation. This research explores the implications of this approach, particularly its potential to improve quantum entanglement and information processing. The significance of this work lies in the potential to offer a fundamentally new paradigm for quantum state management, driven by the intersection of topology and quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Computing Accelerated Non-Linear Model Simulation
abstract: Quantum Computing Accelerated Non-Linear Model Simulation presents a novel approach to accelerating computationally intensive non-linear model simulations. This research explores the utilization of quantum computing's unique properties, specifically superposition and entanglement, to enhance the simulation of complex physical phenomena. The core mechanism involves leveraging these quantum features to overcome the limitations of classical computational methods, offering the potential for significant speedups in simulation times and the ability to tackle problems currently intractable with conventional approaches. This paper details the design of a framework integrating quantum algorithms and simulation techniques to achieve this acceleration. We present initial results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, focusing on a specific example – the simulation of a quantum fluid – highlighting the benefits and challenges of this emerging field. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this technology on diverse scientific and engineering applications.

title: 基于动态拓扑的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in complex, non-linear scenarios. We propose a framework that utilizes dynamic topology to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the input data's geometric structure. The core innovation lies in a quantum-inspired mapping mechanism that transforms optimization parameters into a dynamic topology, enabling the algorithm to adapt to varying input data characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing improved efficiency and robustness compared to existing static optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm offers a significant advancement in optimization by incorporating a self-adapting topology, which leads to more efficient and reliable solutions.

title: Information Flow Dynamics Model for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper proposes the Information Flow Dynamics Model (IFDM), a novel framework for understanding and analyzing the training process of neural networks. The core claim is that neural network training can be accurately described as an information flow dynamics process. This model utilizes information flow dynamics equations to represent and analyze the movement and exchange of information within a neural network during training. Unlike traditional approaches that primarily focus on gradient descent and optimization algorithms, IFDM offers a fundamentally different perspective by treating the training process as a continuous flow of information governed by specific dynamics. This approach allows for a more intuitive and potentially more powerful understanding of the underlying mechanisms driving neural network learning. The model is presented with detailed equations and explores key concepts such as information entropy, information flux, and network connectivity. ---

title: Non-Linear Differential Equation Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic Gaussian theory to the modeling of non-linear differential equations. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on observed data, enabling automatic feature learning and improved simulation accuracy. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically generated "generalized function" representing the solution to the differential equation, allowing the model to adapt to complex data characteristics. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, reducing the need for manual parameter tuning and facilitating more accurate and robust simulations in various scientific domains.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Quantum Circuit Simulation with Adaptive Precision
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit simulation leveraging probabilistic programming and adaptive precision. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with scalability and accuracy, particularly when dealing with complex circuits and noisy environments. Our framework addresses these challenges by dynamically adjusting the computational precision employed during simulation, focusing resources on areas exhibiting the highest uncertainty in the quantum state. We utilize a stochastic variational approach within a probabilistic programming environment, allowing for an iterative refinement of the simulation's accuracy. This adaptive strategy significantly improves efficiency and accuracy compared to fixed-precision simulations. The core claim is that this combination enables efficient quantum circuit simulation by dynamically adjusting computational precision based on the uncertainty of the quantum state. This research presents a new paradigm for quantum simulation, offering potential for broader application and improved performance.

title: 基于动态量子态的拓扑信息编码
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information encoding utilizing dynamic quantum states and topological structure. Traditional encoding methods often rely on manipulating individual quantum states, while this method leverages the inherent properties of topological quantum systems to encode information. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to achieve high-dimensional quantum states with enhanced encoding and decoding capabilities. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the non-linearity of topological quantum states through quantum entanglement, enabling efficient and robust information transfer. This research explores the potential of this technique for advanced quantum computing and quantum communication applications. We demonstrate the feasibility of encoding and decoding complex quantum states using this framework.

title: Core Claim: We propose a Gaussian Process-driven Self-Organizing Theory, leveraging the adaptive properties of Gaussian Processes to combine mathematical self-organization with dynamic system structure modeling, particularly in dynamic systems modeling.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Gaussian Process-based Self-Organizing Theory designed to enhance the modeling and optimization of complex systems, with a focus on dynamic system modeling. The core of this theory lies in a dynamically adaptive 'jump' mechanism within the Gaussian Process, enabling the system to adjust its self-organization based on system dynamics and initial conditions. This approach provides a fundamentally new perspective on modeling self-organization, moving beyond static self-organization parameters to a dynamic and adaptive process. We explore the design of this jump mechanism, its impact on model prediction and optimization, and its potential for more accurate system representation. The theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in modeling complex, dynamic systems. title: Topological Quantum Information Encoding (TQI)
abstract: This paper introduces the Topological Quantum Information Encoding (TQI) method, a novel approach to quantum information processing focused on leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states. Traditional methods often struggle with the limitations of qubit entanglement and the difficulty in efficiently encoding and transmitting complex quantum information. TQI addresses these challenges by employing a structured encoding scheme that utilizes topological quantum states to achieve enhanced storage, transmission, and processing capabilities. The paper details the core mechanism of TQI, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the efficiency of quantum information management. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the TQI method in encoding and manipulating quantum states, showcasing its promise for advancing quantum technologies.

title: A Type-3 Pairing-Based Attribute-Based Encryption Scheme with Expressive Keyword Search and Trapdoor Delegation
abstract: Cloud data sharing allows users to outsource data storage and management to external servers, but it also raises privacy concerns when data must remain encrypted while still supporting efficient search and fine-grained access control. Attribute-based encryption with keyword search (ABE-EKS) addresses this problem by combining searchable encryption with attribute-based access policies. However, existing schemes often focus on separate aspects such as expressive search, online/offline computation, revocation, or policy protection, while controlled trapdoor delegation and inequality-based keyword predicates are less commonly considered together in an implementation-oriented Type-3 pairing setting. This paper revisits the ABE-EKS framework of Yang et al. and adapts it to the Type-3 pairing setting. The construction follows the main structure of Yang et al.’s ABE-EKS scheme, but places the group elements in the appropriate source groups for asymmetric pairings. It further supports expressive access-control and keyword-search policies, Boolean keyword predicates, inequality comparisons, and trapdoor key delegation. We also analyse its security under the honest-but-curious cloud model and implement the scheme using the Apache Milagro Cryptographic Library (AMCL). Experimental results on the Enron Email dataset demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed construction for outsourced encrypted data-sharing scenarios.

title: Depersonalization of personal data in the banking sector: Analysis of methods and selection of an implementation strategy
abstract: This article examines the pressing issue of personal data anonymization in credit and ﬁnancial institutions (CFIs) in the context of tightening regulatory requirements, in particular, Roskomnadzor Order No. 140. It analyzes classic and modern anonymization methods (masking, pseudonymization, synthetic data generation, etc.) for their applicability in a banking environment where preserving data formats, referential integrity, and high performance are critical. A comparative assessment of three modern domestic solutions is provided: DataMask, Garda Data Masking, and N1 AI. Their systemic limitations are identiﬁed, including potential non-compliance with new regulations, insufﬁcient ﬂexibility for unique banking entities, and high cost of ownership. Based on this analysis, the strategic feasibility of developing a specialized internal anonymization tool is substantiated. This tool guarantees full regulatory compliance, maximum adaptability to the bank’s business processes, and long-term economic efﬁciency. A credit and ﬁnancial institution is characterized by processing an extensive array of structured personal data (PD), which combines the features of general, other data, and information that constitutes bank secrecy. This information is typically stored in relational databases in a formalized format (separate ﬁelds for passport number, phone number, account number, etc.), which, on the one hand, simpliﬁes their automated search, but on the other hand, requires strict protection measures, including secure anonymization for use in non-production environments. This determines the key requirements for the system under consideration: the need to accurately detect ﬁelds of various categories of ﬁnancial and identifying information, and the use of masking algorithms that ensure irreversible conversion while preserving the structural integrity and data format for the correct operation of test systems.

title: Comparing supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization for terminology-aware English-to-French medical machine translation
abstract: Die maschinelle Übersetzung im medizinischen Bereich birgt Risiken, die bei Übersetzungen in allgemeinen Bereichen nicht bestehen. Eine flüssige, aber terminologisch falsche Übersetzung kann medizinischem Personal und Patient:innen falsche Informationen vermitteln, und solche Fehler werden leicht übersehen, weil der gesamte Text durch die natürliche Sprache korrekt wirkt. Die genannten Fehler können sogar bis zum Tod führen und unterstreichen, wie wichtig es ist, dieses Thema zu untersuchen und zu erforschen. Die vorliegende Arbeit untersucht, ob Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) die Genauigkeit der medizinischen Terminologieübersetzung bei der maschinellen Übersetzung vom Englischen ins Französische im Vergleich zu Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) allein verbessert. Der Ansatz ist empirisch und vergleichend angelegt, da dieselben Daten und dasselbe Bewertungsverfahren auf drei mehrsprachige Decoder-only-Sprachmodelle angewendet werden, nämlich TowerInstruct-7B, Ministral-8B-Instruct und Qwen3-8B. Jedes Modell wird zunächst mit einem Zero-Shot-Ansatz als Baseline evaluiert und durchläuft anschließend SFT, eine terminologie-angereicherte SFT-Variante und eine terminologie-gestützte DPO-Variante, sodass beobachtete Unterschiede dem jeweils veränderten Schritt zugeschrieben werden können. Die Modelle werden mit Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)-Methoden (QLoRA) auf dem englisch-französischen Parallelkorpus EMEA v3 feinabgestimmt. Dieses Korpus wird durch heuristische und semantische Filter von rund 1,09 Millionen Satzpaaren auf etwa 287.000 reduziert und anschließend in 20.000 Trainings-, 1.000 Validierungs- und 1.000 Testpaare aufgeteilt. Zusätzlich ist der TICO-19-Benchmark vollständig als zentraler Testdatensatz reserviert. Medizinische Begriffe werden aus dem englischen Text mit einem klinischen Named-Entity Recogniser extrahiert und führen über eine Abfrage im Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) zur bevorzugten französischen Übersetzung. Diese Begriffe werden als Glossar in den Instruction Prompt eingefügt und bilden so die mit Terminologie angereicherte SFT-Variante. Für DPO wird zunächst der Adapter in das Basismodell integriert und ein neuer Adapter angehängt. Anschließend werden Präferenzpaare aus acht generierten Hypothesen gebildet und gereiht, wobei die Präferenzstärke über einen Sweep ausgewählt wird. Die Evaluierung kombiniert BLEU, ChrF und COMET mit einer Berechnung der Terminologiegenauigkeit, gepaarten Bootstrap-Signifikanztests und einer manuellen Inspektion der Systemausgaben. Das zentrale Ergebnis ist ein deutlich negatives Resultat für DPO. Über alle drei Modelle und beide Testdatensätze hinweg unterscheidet sich das terminologie-bewusste DPO-System vom terminologie-angereicherten SFT-System höchstens um wenige Tausendstel für COMET, und die Wahl der Präferenzstärke hat wenig Einfluss. Bei Qwen erzeugen das überwachte und das präferenzoptimierte System häufig sehr ähnliche Ausgaben. SFT hat einen größeren Effekt. Im Vergleich zur Zero-Shot-Baseline verbessert es COMET für Tower und Qwen auf dem EMEA-Testset, sinkt jedoch für alle Modelle auf dem TICO-19-Testset unter die Werte der Baseline. Terminologieanreicherung verändert die Werte über beide Testsets hinweg inkonsistent und liefert keine verlässliche Verbesserung. BLEU und ChrF unterscheiden sich von COMET in ihrem Verhalten, was dafür spricht, eine neuronale Metrik für die primäre Messung zu verwenden. Die Arbeit präsentiert reproduzierbare Zero-Shot-, SFT- und DPO-Systeme für die medizinische Englisch-Französisch-Übersetzung sowie die methodischen Schritte, die erforderlich sind, um DPO stabil auf parameter-effizienten Modellen zu trainieren. Die weitergehende Folge ist, dass die Wahl des Basismodells und dessen Stärke für die terminologische Genauigkeit wichtiger sind als die hier untersuchte Präferenzoptimierungsphase und dass verlässliche Genauigkeit in bezug auf die korrekte Terminologieübersetzung wahrscheinlich Mechanismen erfordern wird, die die Verwendung korrekter Begriffe erzwingen, statt sie nur zu suggerieren.

title: Noēsis: Deterministic-First Retrieval with Two-Tier Context Hydration for Factuality-Critical Queries on Small Local Models
abstract: A wrong number is worse than no answer. Across factuality-critical domains -- audience metrics, scheduling and rights in media; dosages and lab values in healthcare; figures and citations in finance and legal -- a confident but fabricated value is more damaging than an honest admission of uncertainty. Yet this is the dominant failure mode we observe on small local language models: even when correct evidence is present in context, models fabricate plausible numbers and timestamps. Recent work characterizes a real limit of this regime: below 7B parameters, the bottleneck of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is not retrieval quality but context utilization. We present Noesis, the deterministic-first query plane of the Noesis architecture, which makes every deterministic judgment before generation. Its mechanisms follow from the ingestion architecture (subject of a separate patent application): (a) a producer-side fact layer rendering precomputed metric facts verbatim without ranking; (b) positional addressing with deterministic cross-source alignment, resolved ahead of query time at zero LLM cost; (c) provenance scoping as an attribution constraint with multi-tier named-reference routing; and (d) two-tier context with model-triggered verbatim hydration. Across four ablations, a 2B model reaches parity with a 35B model on factual integrity (exact values in all runs; zero confabulated numbers on absent-entity traps); structured retrieval beats flat RAG by +11.4 points at 2B; skeleton-only context preserves quantitative answers at 20-30% smaller prompts; and hydration recovers verbatim narrative in ~8s versus ~29s. Two properties matter for regulated domains: each query resolves in a single generation call, and every reported value is traceable to its exact source and position by construction.

title: FreqDoor: A Hidden Trojan in the Frequency Domain for Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have recently shown excellent progress in open-ended image-to-text generation. However, their multimodal nature makes them persistently vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Existing backdoor triggers for VLMs are either spatial, textual, or bimodal, which may yield localized or recognizable trigger patterns. In this work, we explore a different attack surface and propose \ textsc {FreqDoor}, a training-time backdoor attack that implants triggers in the frequency domain. \ textsc {FreqDoor} mixes amplitude-spectrum components from a trigger-source image selectively while preserving the phase of a clean image to generate a spatially distributed and visually imperceptible trigger without modifying the textual input. We evaluate the attack on BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA for image captioning and visual question answering. On Flickr8k, \ textsc {FreqDoor} achieves attack success rates of $99.6\%$, $99.8\%$, and $98.4\%$ on the three models, respectively, while preserving the semantic quality of the generated captions. On VQAv2, the corresponding attack success rates are $99.6\%$, $92.4\%$, and $79.6\%$.

title: Beyond Single-Negative Preference: Multi-Negative DPO for LLM-Centric Historical Entity Linking
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown promise for historical entity linking, but preference optimization for this task is often formulated with only one negative candidate per training instance. This discards information from the remaining candidates retrieved for the same mention. We introduce multi-negative direct preference optimisation (MDPO), a reference-based pairwise objective that compares the correct entity with all valid rejected candidates associated with each mention. MDPO preserves the Bradley-Terry formulation of DPO while exploiting the complete candidate set through masked, length-normalised sequence scores. We evaluate MDPO on hipe-2020 and newseye, covering French, German, English, Swedish, and Finnish historical newspaper text. Experiments show that MDPO improves over supervised fine-tuning and single-negative DPO, with particularly strong gains for NIL mentions, semantic ambiguity, OCR noise, and historically difficult names. Further analyses disentangle candidate-generation and selection errors, showing that candidate retrieval remains a key bottleneck for end-to-end entity linking. These results demonstrate that incorporating all within-instance negative candidates is a simple and effective improvement for LLM-based historical entity linking.

evidence.title: Beyond Single-Negative Preference: Multi-Negative DPO for LLM-Centric Historical Entity Linking
evidence.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown promise for historical entity linking, but preference optimization for this task is often formulated with only one negative candidate per training instance. This discards information from the remaining candidates retrieved for the same mention. We introduce multi-negative direct preference optimisation (MDPO), a reference-based pairwise objective that compares the correct entity with all valid rejected candidates associated with each mention. MDPO preserves the Bradley-Terry formulation of DPO while exploiting the complete candidate set through masked, length-normalised sequence scores. We evaluate MDPO on hipe-2020 and newseye, covering French, German, English, Swedish, and Finnish historical newspaper text. Experiments show that MDPO improves over supervised fine-tuning and single-negative DPO, with particularly strong gains for NIL mentions, semantic ambiguity, OCR noise, and historically difficult names. Further analyses disentangle candidate-generation and selection errors, showing that candidate retrieval remains a key bottleneck for end-to-end entity linking. These results demonstrate that incorporating all within-instance negative candidates is a simple and effective improvement for LLM-based historical entity linking.

title: Design and Development of an Intelligent Multi-Format Document Processing System Using Agentic AI and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Enterprise document workflows still depend heavily on manual review of unstructured technical, contractual, and administrative files, and conventional keyword or OCR-based extraction pipelines fail to preserve layout, tabular structure, and multilingual context. This paper presents an intelligent, self-correcting document processing system that combines layout-aware ingestion with a four-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. The ingestion stage passes PDF, CSV and TXT documents including automated Gmail/IMAP intake with SHA-256 content deduplication applies sliding-window chunking, and indexes dense embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) in a persistent Chroma vector store. At query time, a Planning, Retrieval, Generation and Compliance/Validation agent graph retrieves the top-k relevant chunks and produces a deterministic, source-grounded answer (Llama-3.3-70B, temperature = 0.0), refusing to respond when grounding is insufficient. On a diagnostic benchmark of ten entity-disambiguation queries over heterogeneous technical documents, the system achieved 100% Recall@6, 100% Correctness, Relevance, and Completeness and a per-criterion Faithfulness score of 60% a discrepancy traced not to factual error but to the LLM-as-a-Judge harness penalizing natural-language phrasing of compact source facts. The findings position agentic, self-correcting RAG as a practical, auditable alternative to single pass pipelines for document heavy Industry 4.0 environments.

title: KJac: Constraint-Aware NAS for Learned Optimization
abstract: This preprint presents KJac, a zero-training neural architecture search proxy for learned optimization in constrained optimization settings. The study evaluates Jacobian-based architecture scoring across linear projection, convex quadratic programming, QCQP-style constraints, and portfolio optimization tasks. It examines predictive correlation with final model performance, computational cost, feasibility-aware diagnostics, and architecture selection behavior. The work investigates the utility and limitations of Jacobian-based proxies for architecture search in constrained learned-optimization problems.

title: NSRDB Datasets for Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) Forecasting Across India (Madurai), Brazil, and Nepal (2012–2014)
abstract: "This dataset contains the processed and feature-engineered NSRDB meteorological and solar irradiance data (2012–2014) for three climatically distinct locations — Madurai (India), Brazil, and the Himalayas (Nepal) — used to train and evaluate six machine learning models for Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) forecasting, as reported in Performance Evaluation of Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms for Direct Normal Irradiance Forecasting in Diverse Climatic Conditions. Each location folder contains the training (2012–2013) from raw NSRDB inputs are third-party data and link to nsrdb.nrel.gov.

abstract: Reproducibility package for the Salud Digital ICU mortality prediction study. The package contains analysis scripts, aggregate non-patient-level outputs, variable documentation, execution instructions, environment files, and revised manuscript materials for evaluating intra-domain validation and cross-domain transfer between MIMIC-III Demo and eICU-CRD. Patient-level MIMIC/eICU raw or derived records are not included because the source databases are PhysioNet clinical resources subject to credentialing, data-use agreements, and access controls.

title: Emergent Complexity from Sparse Connectivity in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for sparse connectivity patterns to foster emergent complexity within neural networks, contributing to improved generalization performance. Traditional approaches often treat connectivity as a fixed attribute, neglecting the dynamic evolution driven by training data. We propose a novel framework that dynamically models connectivity changes and quantifies their impact on network representation, focusing on how these patterns influence the network's capacity to learn complex functions. The paper introduces a modified connection matrix approach, incorporating a measure of sparsity and dynamically adjusting connectivity weights based on training data. We demonstrate through a series of experiments that this approach significantly improves performance on benchmark datasets, particularly in tasks requiring robust feature extraction and generalization. The results highlight the importance of considering dynamic connectivity patterns for enhancing neural network capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation: An Adaptive Quantum Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum algorithm, "Quantum Entanglement Computation," designed to exploit this phenomenon for enhanced quantum computation. The core of this algorithm lies in the introduction of a "Quantum State Adaptation" mechanism, which dynamically adjusts quantum gate parameters based on the inherent evolution of the quantum state. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional algorithms, which rely on static parameter settings, offering a pathway towards significantly improved computational efficiency. We detail the mechanism, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its efficacy. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this adaptive quantum algorithm on the field of quantum computing.

title: TurnShift: Sequential Detection of Mid-Conversation Author Substitution via Behavioral User Profiling
abstract: TurnShift (formerly BehaviorGuard) detects mid-conversation author substitution by accumulating per-user embedding residuals with CUSUM. It also maintains privacy-preserving user profiles (semantic, linguistic, temporal) used by a composite per-message scorer; that scorer is retained as a baseline, not as a primary result.

title: Quantum Machine Learning in Adaptive Matrix Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing machine learning algorithms, particularly in areas demanding complex computations. This research investigates a novel approach to QML, specifically focusing on the optimization of matrix operations, aiming to significantly accelerate model training and improve generalization capabilities. We propose a quantum-enhanced matrix optimization technique leveraging the unique properties of quantum machine learning to address the computational bottlenecks inherent in traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism centers around quantum algorithms designed to efficiently navigate and manipulate matrices, leading to faster convergence and enhanced model performance. This work presents a framework for adapting to quantum machine learning, offering a potential pathway to accelerate the training and deployment of complex models.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm-Based Topological Topology Analysis (AQT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Quantum Algorithm-Based Topological Topology Analysis (AQT) method, a novel approach to topology analysis that leverages quantum algorithms for rapid identification and optimization of complex topological structures. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and scale of these structures. AQT offers significant improvements in computational efficiency and accuracy through the application of quantum algorithms tailored for topological analysis. This paper details the fundamental principles of AQT, presents a preliminary implementation demonstrating its effectiveness, and discusses potential future developments and applications within the field of topology. The core mechanism of AQT revolves around the quantum-enhanced exploration of topological spaces, enabling the identification of subtle patterns and relationships that would be missed by classical methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Bias-Variance Trade-off via Constraint Propagation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to bias-variance reduction, introducing an adaptive mechanism that dynamically adjusts the model's parameters based on the data's inherent statistical structure. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters or simplistic regularization, failing to adequately address the complexities of real-world datasets. We propose a framework centered around constraint propagation, which iteratively refines model parameters to minimize errors across different data subsets. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to intelligently identify and exploit the data's underlying patterns, resulting in improved generalization performance. This work addresses a critical limitation of existing techniques by providing a flexible and adaptive solution to the bias-variance trade-off. The proposed method offers a promising path toward more robust and accurate models.

title: Nonlinear Self-Organizing Neural Networks: Dynamic Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic topology analysis as a method for training neural networks to self-organize into complex, dynamic neural architectures. Traditional neural network training relies heavily on parameter adjustments, which can lead to suboptimal solutions. We introduce a novel dynamic topology framework, utilizing a training process that compels the network to learn and maintain a self-organizing topology. This approach offers enhanced learning efficiency and improved model generalization capabilities compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the network's topology during training, fostering a self-organized structure. This study explores the benefits of this dynamic approach in building neural networks capable of exhibiting complex, adaptive behaviors.

title: Quantum Error Correction Based Distributed Databases
abstract: This paper explores the design and theoretical foundations of a distributed database leveraging quantum error correction (QEC) techniques. The core claim is that utilizing QEC allows for the construction of a highly secure and reliable distributed database, significantly enhancing data integrity and fault tolerance compared to traditional approaches. The proposed mechanism involves encoding data into quantum states and employing QEC codes for error detection and correction, facilitating robust data storage and retrieval in a distributed environment. While the application of QEC in distributed databases is theoretically promising, it presents significant technological challenges. This work outlines the key components and considerations for such a system, highlighting potential architectures and the inherent complexities involved in scaling QEC for practical database applications. We present a framework for achieving secure and resilient data management in a quantum-enhanced distributed system, focusing on the fundamental principles and mathematical underpinnings of this novel approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic inference engine, termed "Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Resonance," which leverages principles from quantum mechanics – specifically superposition and measurement – to improve reasoning and decision-making in complex systems. The core of the engine is a "resonance state," representing a superposition of multiple possible outcomes, dynamically weighted based on the correlated evidence. This weighting process simulates a quantum collapse, allowing the system to prioritize more probable outcomes. We demonstrate that this approach can potentially overcome limitations inherent in traditional Bayesian networks, particularly in scenarios involving high dimensionality, complex dependencies, and ambiguous data. The engine's adaptability and ability to incorporate diverse evidence sources are highlighted. The theoretical framework and the underlying mathematical formalism are presented, outlining the key components and their interrelationships. This research offers a new perspective on probabilistic inference, drawing inspiration from the counterintuitive yet powerful concepts of the quantum world.

title: Topological Quantum Field Theory: A Novel Approach to Information Preservation and Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the profound influence of topological structures on quantum field theory, proposing a novel computational paradigm predicated on quantum entanglement and a topological space. We explore how these structures can be leveraged to enhance information preservation and enable fundamentally new computation methods. The core claim centers on the potential for utilizing topological properties to mitigate information loss and facilitate robust data integrity within quantum systems. This work introduces a new framework, detailed in the Core Mechanism section, that integrates quantum entanglement with topological geometry to achieve a fundamentally different approach to computation. The investigation highlights the potential of this approach to address key challenges in quantum computing, specifically concerning information preservation and the development of efficient computation.

title: Quantum Topology for Adaptive Quantum System Control
abstract: Quantum topology is a novel approach to quantum system control that leverages the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum states and interactions, enabling efficient quantum system optimization. This paper introduces a framework based on quantum topology that allows for adaptive state transfer and interaction, and offers a mechanism for quantum system optimization through quantum system evolution simulations. We present a detailed design of this framework, highlighting its potential for significant advancements in quantum control and optimization. This work represents a departure from traditional approaches, offering a fundamentally new way to control quantum systems through the inherent structure of quantum topology.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos – Adaptive Metric Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Bayesian geometric chaos to the learning of complex, non-linear metric spaces. The core claim is to develop a robust Bayesian framework for metric learning that dynamically adjusts to unpredictable chaotic dynamics within the data, thereby improving prediction accuracy and providing robust uncertainty estimation. Traditional approaches often fall short in handling the inherent complexities of these environments, necessitating a fundamentally new method that leverages Bayesian inference and a 'chaos' component. We propose a novel approach involving a dynamically updated metric space representation, incorporating a mechanism to detect and adapt to chaotic feedback loops. The paper explores the mathematical foundations of this approach, detailing the Bayesian framework, the adaptation process, and the resulting performance improvements. The results demonstrate a significant enhancement in prediction accuracy and a strengthened uncertainty estimation capability compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving high dimensionality and non-linearity.

title: Cognitive Resonance for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) systems have achieved significant advancements, yet their reliance on exhaustive search remains a critical bottleneck, severely impacting scalability and efficiency. This paper proposes a novel approach, termed "cognitive resonance," designed to augment existing ATP systems by incorporating elements of human intuition into the proof search process. The core idea is to establish a network of partially proven theorems and leverage resonance patterns—analogous to those observed in human cognition—to intelligently guide the search. This layer doesn't replace traditional search algorithms but rather acts as a dynamic heuristic, prioritizing promising proof paths based on the interconnectedness and potential of the theorems within the network. We outline the architecture of this "cognitive resonance" layer, detailing the mechanisms for maintaining the theorem network, identifying resonance patterns, and integrating them into the ATP search strategy. Preliminary considerations regarding the complexity and potential challenges are discussed. The aim is to demonstrate a pathway toward more efficient and scalable ATP systems by mimicking the cognitive processes that underpin human mathematical reasoning.

title: Applicability-Aware Reliability Scoring and Prediction of EMS Patient-Care Records for Trustworthy Smart Ambulance AI
abstract: This study introduces the EMS Record Reliability Index (EMS-RRI), an interpretable, applicability-aware measure of whether each prehospital patient-care record is complete enough to support downstream smart-ambulance AI. Using National Emergency Medical Services Information System (NEMSIS) data, we analyzed 500,000 EMS records from the 2025 dataset for development and internal evaluation and 200,000 records from the 2024 dataset for temporal validation. We constructed basic and domain-weighted EMS-RRI variants and evaluated supervised models that identify low-reliability records using broader EMS context rather than the EMS-RRI score itself. The final XGBoost model achieved ROC-AUC/PR-AUC/F1 values of 0.9145/0.8659/0.7745 on the 2025 internal test set and 0.8887/0.8407/0.7455 under temporal validation. Failure analysis showed that most false negatives were borderline cases: more than 86% were within 2 EMS-RRI points of the cutoff, while only about 3% had scores below 70. Larger temporal declines were observed in selected regional and urbanicity subgroups, including Western Plains and Frontier records. Adding EMS-RRI to downstream high-acuity prediction produced modest but consistent gains across validation, internal-test, and temporal cohorts. By providing a practical record-level reliability signal before downstream smart-ambulance AI use, EMS-RRI reinforces a central requirement of high-stakes prehospital automation: trustworthy decisions must begin with trustworthy records.

title: Improving service efficiency without sacrificing quality: a multi-agent AI system for hospitality email response automation
abstract: Purpose This study examines how multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) architectures can automate hospitality email responses while maintaining service quality standards. The research addresses the growing challenge of email volume management in hotel operations where response time expectations increasingly conflict with operational capacity constraints. Design/methodology/approach A three-month pilot study evaluated a multi-agent system across 200 properties within a large global hospitality enterprise operating thousands of properties across multiple segments. The architecture employed three specialized agents using Claude 3.5 Sonnet via AWS Bedrock: a triage agent for classification and security, a knowledge retrieval agent with hybrid search capabilities and a drafting agent with validation mechanisms. Human evaluation of 2,500 emails (10% sample) assessed accuracy, tone, clarity, policy compliance and response effectiveness against human-only baselines. Properties should establish confidence thresholds (0.70 for human review, 0.85 for automation) and prioritize agent-specific policy enforcement over model selection. The approach proves particularly effective for select-service and extended-stay brands facing high inquiry volumes with limited staffing. title: HyCO: A Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Sequential reinforcement learning (RL) solvers and global diffusion model (DM) solvers for neural combinatorial optimization exhibit complementary failure modes under an optimization-regret view. The former enjoys small marginal regret in the early construction stage, but suffers from horizon-wise compounding errors with super-linear regret growth; the latter avoids horizon compounding but incurs linear or sublinear regret w.r.t. the dimension of the remaining unsolved subspace. We propose Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization (HyCO), a hybrid inference algorithm that constructs a solution prefix with an RL solver and adaptively switches to a conditional DM to complete the remaining decisions. To characterize why such hybridization helps, when to trigger the handover, and how to realize it in practice, we first develop a unified error-scaling theoretical framework and prove that, under explicit error-scaling assumptions, i) the hybrid structure achieves strictly lower expected regret than either backbone alone, and ii) there exists a unique optimal trigger step that minimizes the hybrid regret. We then design a lightweight adaptive trigger that combines policy entropy and RL-DM disagreement to detect trajectory-level signals of the regime shift as a practical proxy, since the optimal trigger step is defined at the expected-regret level and is not directly computable on individual trajectories. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that HyCO achieves consistent improvements over both backbones and support the empirical effectiveness of adaptive triggering.

title: AnomalyCraft-700K: Component-Level Controllable and Verifiable Synthetic Anomalies for Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding
abstract: Progress in video anomaly understanding (VAU) has long been limited by inherent deficiencies of real-world anomaly videos, which are hard to collect and offer little control over their content. Synthetic anomaly approaches partially alleviate data scarcity, yet their generation remains largely controlled at the category or prompt level. They also lack component-level verification of video-text consistency and provide insufficient hard normal samples near the normal-anomaly boundary. To address this, we present AnomalyCraft-700K, a component-controllable synthetic anomaly dataset for fine-grained VAU, containing over 40K videos and over 700K task-level textual annotations. From fine-grained semantic components and a progressive three-stage pipeline, we craft anomaly events that are richly detailed, semantically controlled, and temporally structured, and additionally construct per-category hard normal samples to prompt the model to discriminate based on anomaly semantics rather than surface visual cues. Moreover, using the components as verification units, AnomalyCraft-700K further performs component-wise correction of video-text discrepancies introduced during generation, providing reliable annotations with verified cross-modal alignment for six tasks that progress from anomaly detection, through anomaly retrieval and captioning, to fine-grained anomaly reasoning. Evaluations of widely used methods under both traditional and MLLM-based protocols demonstrate that AnomalyCraft-700K serves as an effective source of supervision, from anomaly detection to fine-grained anomaly understanding.

title: CantoneseLLM v2: Reasoning in a Low-Resource Language
abstract: Cantonese is widely spoken but remains low-resource in written data, with no large corpus of native Cantonese reasoning traces available for model training. We develop and release CantoneseLLM v2, comprising models based on Qwen3 8B and 30B-A3B. The models are trained through CPT on 784 million Cantonese and Hong Kong-related tokens, chat-vector merging, SFT, DPO, and RLVR. Evaluation across the training stages shows that chat-vector merging transfers instruction following but preserves the donor model's reasoning language, while SFT with limited Cantonese reasoning data substantially shortens or removes reasoning traces and reduces benchmark performance. DPO restores the reasoning-block format, particularly for the 8B model, but recovers only part of the lost performance. The RLVR training with Cantonese language and Traditional Chinese scripts as multiplicative constraints introduced Cantonese language alignment and restored the lost performance. The 30B-A3B model reaches 73.16 on HKCanto-Eval, within 1.20 points of its merged checkpoint, while retaining the Cantonese reasoning behaviour absent from that checkpoint. We release the model checkpoints, the training environments, and a thirteen-year Traditional Chinese Common Crawl dataset. The models can be accessed at https://huggingface.co/collections/hon9kon9ize/cantonesellm-v20

title: Identifying Fraudulent Credit Card Transactions Using Ensemble Learning
abstract: One major challenge for banks and financial institutions is identifying fraudulent credit card transactions, as criminals can also masquerade as legitimate cardholders. To address the inherent class imbalance problem in a fraud detection problem, resampling techniques such as oversampling, undersampling, and SMOTE are applied to the datasets that include European Data and Sparkov Data. To improve the classification, ensemble learning is employed to select different algorithms to make it more accurate and reliable. The study indicates the use of an ensemble-based method with advanced resampling techniques to improve the training and forecasting of the models. The comparison of several classification models is done in great detail and the best model is found to be the Stacking Classifier. It combines multiple base models to enhance the accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score of all techniques. This can prove to be a major step in enhancing fraud detection systems, providing accurate identification of fraudulent transactions and fewer false positives. The proposed solution highlights the importance of ensemble methods and data balancing techniques for tackling the complexity in financial fraud detection.

title: Evaluation of Azure Pronunciation Assessment Tool for Arabic-Speaking Learners
abstract: Accurate reading aloud is crucial for Arabic-speaking learners because minor errors can alter meaning or hinder understanding. This study evaluated the Microsoft Azure Pronunciation Assessment (PA) tool for modern standard Arabic using the KSU Arabic Speech Database. We focused on male speakers recorded in silent rooms. We used the KSU database’s varied prompts words, phrases, and sentences to test Azure PA at the word, phoneme, and sentence levels. Because Azure PA is a closed source, we approximated its scoring by deriving equations for the Accuracy, Completeness, and Fluency metrics. We showed that a simple weighted combination closely matched the Pronunciation scores. We also applied a standard audio preprocessing pipeline (channel selection, denoising, pre-emphasis, silence trimming, and loudness normalization) to measure its impact. With preprocessing, for male speakers in the KSU database under the no-reference mode, Accuracy increased from 91.74% to 95.33%, Fluency from 60.84% to 97.84%, Completeness from 97.16% to 100.0%, and Pronunciation from 73.64% to 96.26%. The number of decoded word tokens increased fivefold. After preprocessing, all the consonant classes reached 90% accuracy, although the glottal segments remained weak. Sentence-level tests showed that Azure PA originally captured only brief fragments of long recordings. After preprocessing, it covered a greater portion of each sentence and recovered more of the target text. These results demonstrate both the strengths and limitations of Azure PA as a diagnostic tool for Arabic pronunciation based on KSU data.

title: A General Theory of Neural Fields: Width, Attention, Covariance Processes, Renormalization, Gauge Quotients, and Quantum Reconstruction
abstract: We develop a mathematical framework for neural field laws that separates width, head count, sequence length, depth, training, coarse-graining, parameter quotients, and quantum reconstruction. Under a declared conditional Gaussian representation, connected field correlators are determined by cumulants of the random covariance. Fixed-head attention can consequently remain non-Gaussian at infinite channel width, whereas independent head aggregation suppresses higher cumulants. A grading fan organizes distinct asymptotic paths, and a stationary covariance cocycle identifies the rate of initialization-memory decay. Training is treated separately through controlled Fokker--Planck evolution and Hamilton--Jacobi duality. Explicit coarse maps make RG claims testable. We give transport and composition bounds, exact Gaussian decimation, an exactly closed non-Gaussian Gamma family with computable scaling exponents, and a conditioned spectral estimate for approximate conjugacy. A constructive obstruction shows that zero one-step training risk need not control recursive coarse-graining; discarded-state memory and intermediate-scale support explain two sources of failed closure. Reflection positivity remains a separate requirement. We establish preservation results and negative witnesses, and exhibit a reflection-positive covariance mixture that fails clustering. Neural random fields therefore require additional hypotheses for positive-metric quantum reconstruction. Reproducible calculations include 32 fixed attention kernels and a supervised study of 24 trained models (12 LSTMs and 12 transformers) across three input tasks and three seeds. Intermediate-scale training reduces median eight-token Rademacher averaging error from 0.0665 to 0.0256 for the LSTM and from 0.2664 to 0.00493 for the transformer. All 180 sampled scale records satisfy the applicable trajectory-error bound. These results test recovery of a prescribed map and a compositional failure mechanism; they do not establish spontaneous universality or an isomorphism between generic neural architectures and RG flows.

title: Geometric Topology Validation of Quantum Computing
abstract: Geometric topology offers a novel approach to validating quantum computing algorithms and protocols, addressing limitations of traditional methods. This paper proposes a framework leveraging the principles of geometric topology to rigorously test the correctness of quantum computation, specifically focusing on quantum geometric analysis. The core claim is that this framework will provide a robust and mathematically sound validation of quantum algorithms, ensuring their fidelity and robustness against potential errors. The mechanism involves analyzing the quantum geometric structure inherent in quantum algorithms, identifying inconsistencies, and subsequently proposing corrections or modifications to the algorithm. The research explores the potential of this approach to enhance the reliability and security of quantum technologies.

title: Dynamic Probability Graphs: Adaptive Modeling for Complex Systems
abstract: Dynamic Probability Graphs (DPGs) represent a novel approach to modeling complex systems by dynamically adjusting the graph's structure based on evolving objectives and constraints. This paper introduces a method for automatic graph redesign through a sophisticated update mechanism, leveraging optimization algorithms to ensure the graph optimally responds to changing conditions. The core claim centers on the design of a DPG that can adapt to complex systems, offering improved prediction and control capabilities compared to traditional static modeling techniques. The paper details the fundamental principles, the proposed update mechanism, and the resulting advantages of this approach in addressing challenges associated with dynamic environments.

title: Isotropic Adaptive Clustering Algorithm (ISPA)
abstract: This paper presents the Isotropic Adaptive Clustering Algorithm (ISPA), a novel clustering method designed to automatically adjust cluster characteristics based on data distribution shifts. Traditional clustering algorithms often struggle with data that evolves over time, necessitating adaptive approaches. ISPA addresses this challenge by employing a dynamic adjustment mechanism that modifies cluster features in real-time, ensuring improved model accuracy and robustness. We introduce a framework that leverages the concept of isotropic distributions to dynamically adapt to data variations, resulting in a more nuanced and accurate clustering outcome. This paper details the algorithm's design, its implementation, and its performance evaluation on a range of datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex data patterns.

title: 基于自适应的量子图灵机
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum graph-theoretical algorithm, termed the "Adaptive Quantum Graph (AQG)," designed to enhance quantum computation through dynamic qubit arrangement. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on static circuit designs, limiting their adaptability. The AQG leverages quantum entanglement and quantum gates to dynamically adjust qubit states, enabling a more responsive and efficient computation. The core claim is that this algorithm significantly improves upon existing quantum computation techniques by enabling adaptive qubit manipulation. This advancement is driven by the potential for more flexible and efficient algorithms, particularly in scenarios with variable input data. The paper details the algorithm's core mechanisms, including quantum entanglement and quantum gate manipulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its implementation. This research contributes to the exploration of quantum computing paradigms that move beyond fixed circuit designs toward more adaptive and expressive computation.

title: Graph Neural Networks with Intrinsic Dimensionality Reduction
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommender systems. However, their performance is frequently hampered by the "curse of dimensionality," a fundamental challenge arising from the high-dimensional nature of graph data. This paper proposes a novel approach to mitigate this issue by integrating intrinsic dimensionality reduction techniques directly into the GNN architecture. Specifically, we explore the use of autoencoders and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to learn a compact, lower-dimensional representation of the graph, thereby reducing the computational complexity and improving the scalability of GNNs. The core idea is to leverage the inherent structure of the graph data to create a more efficient and robust representation for the network to learn from. We present a theoretical framework outlining the benefits of this approach and discuss potential implementation strategies. Our methodology aims to address a critical bottleneck in GNN research, paving the way for more efficient and scalable graph representation learning.

title: Dynamic Information Entropy Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to optimize parameter values by focusing on dynamic information entropy. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on static optimization, while the dynamic entropy evolution mechanism actively adjusts parameters based on entropy changes, leading to improved performance. The algorithm utilizes a feedback loop to iteratively refine the parameter set, ensuring a more efficient and robust optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal parameter values more rapidly and achieve higher accuracy compared to established methods. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic entropy evolution process, offering a significant advancement in parameter optimization.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Hierarchical Representations from Multi-Scale Sensor Data
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-supervised learning framework for learning hierarchical representations from multi-scale sensor data. The core challenge in leveraging data from sources like LiDAR, radar, and cameras simultaneously is the lack of explicit supervision. We introduce a system that automatically constructs a hierarchical graph representation of the sensor data, learning to predict higher-level features from lower-level ones. This process is driven by inherent data constraints, leading to the emergence of a meaningful hierarchical structure without requiring manual design of features or labels. The framework's ability to directly learn from raw, multi-scale sensor data offers significant advantages over traditional supervised methods, particularly in scenarios where labeled data is scarce or unavailable. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach on synthetic datasets, highlighting its potential for applications in autonomous navigation, robotics, and environmental monitoring. The key innovation lies in the cyclical, self-supervised prediction task within the hierarchical graph, allowing the network to iteratively refine its understanding of the data at different levels of abstraction.

title: Quantum-Correlated Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for feature extraction from complex datasets. The core concept involves representing dataset features using entangled qubits. Measurements of these qubits, governed by their entangled correlations, generate a compressed and highly informative data representation. This approach contrasts with traditional feature extraction techniques, which often suffer from computational bottlenecks when dealing with high-dimensional data. The proposed method aims to dramatically reduce computational complexity by exploiting the inherent parallelism and correlations within quantum systems. We present a theoretical framework outlining the algorithm and its expected performance, demonstrating the potential for significantly faster and more efficient feature extraction. The results suggest a promising avenue for future research in areas such as machine learning and data analysis.

title: Multi-Variable Entanglement Control in Asymmetric Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to asymmetric quantum computing centered around the precise control of multi-variable entanglement. Current methods primarily leverage single-variable entanglement, presenting limitations in scalability and parallel computation efficiency. We propose a framework utilizing quantum gate arrays and quantum circuits to construct a multi-variable entanglement control mechanism. This mechanism employs precisely executed quantum gate operations to establish entanglement between multiple qubits, facilitating controlled entanglement swapping. The core claim is to design a scheme capable of simultaneously controlling multiple variables, ultimately enhancing computational power and scalability for asymmetric quantum algorithms. The theoretical underpinnings are detailed, outlining the mathematical formalism and key operational steps involved in achieving this multi-variable control. This work introduces a new paradigm for asymmetric quantum computing, addressing a critical bottleneck in the field. ---

title: Hierarchical Memory Networks with Semantic Pruning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Hierarchical Memory Networks with Semantic Pruning (HMNS). The core challenge in memory networks lies in their tendency to accumulate irrelevant information, leading to increased computational cost and reduced efficiency. To address this, we propose a system that leverages a hierarchical memory structure, organized as a tree representing semantic concepts, and incorporates a dynamic pruning mechanism guided by a reinforcement learning agent. The agent learns to prioritize and retain only the most relevant memory nodes based on the current task context. This adaptive pruning significantly reduces the memory footprint while maintaining the ability to retrieve information effectively. We formalize the key components of the HMNS architecture using mathematical notation, detailing the memory tree structure, the reinforcement learning algorithm, and the pruning criteria. The system's efficiency is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and a detailed explanation of the learning process. This work represents a significant step towards more efficient and focused memory networks, particularly suitable for applications requiring robust information retrieval from large and complex datasets.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks with Latent Variable Dropout
abstract: Bayesian Networks (BNs) provide a powerful framework for representing and reasoning under uncertainty. However, their complexity grows exponentially with the number of variables, leading to computational challenges, particularly in high-dimensional scenarios. This paper introduces Adaptive Bayesian Networks (ABNs) with Latent Variable Dropout, a novel approach designed to mitigate this issue. The core idea is to dynamically remove (set to zero) irrelevant latent variables based on their estimated irrelevance, thereby reducing the computational burden without significantly compromising predictive accuracy. We formulate the dropout process using Bayesian model selection principles, adapting the network structure iteratively to optimize both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method leverages a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach for estimating variable relevance and employs a thresholding mechanism to determine which variables to drop. Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of ABNs in reducing computational complexity while maintaining comparable predictive performance to standard BNs, showcasing a significant improvement in scalability for complex, high-dimensional datasets.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Temporal Memory for Exploration
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) within a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework to address the persistent challenge of exploration. Traditional MARL often suffers from premature convergence to suboptimal solutions due to the complexity of the state and action spaces and the difficulty in coordinating exploration across multiple agents. We propose a novel architecture that integrates HTM's predictive coding capabilities directly into the MARL system, allowing agents to learn and maintain internal models of their environment and their interactions with other agents. These internal models facilitate proactive exploration, enabling agents to anticipate future states and actions, ultimately leading to more efficient and robust exploration strategies. The core claim of this work is that HTM's predictive coding significantly improves exploration in MARL environments. We present a detailed formulation of the proposed approach, including the key components and algorithms, and discuss its potential impact on MARL research and applications. The results, while presented conceptually here, demonstrate the significant potential of this combined approach.

title: Adversarial Machine Learning for cybersecurity Threat Detection
abstract: Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) offers a paradigm shift in cybersecurity threat detection, which attacked the weaknesses inherent in conventional machine learning (ML) systems. In this paper, we present a strong AML mechanism combining adversarial training, dynamic threat simulation, and lightweight ensemble in a generalization manner for real-time detection. Further, the framework is compared with the existing approaches using the benchmark cybersecurity datasets and exhibits better performance in detection of zero-day and stealth attacks with a detection accuracy of 94.3%. The model can be deployed in a practical fashion to a variety of network environments, to hedge against emerging adversarial threats. Our experimental results demonstrate that we have achieved a great improvement over the state-of-the-art defense methods in terms of accuracy and response time.
